items.title: Apple downgraded at Jefferies over iPhone yields and growth concerns
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Tech Editor Dan Howley breaks down Jefferies' downgrade of Apple (AAPL) to 'underperform' following reports of a canceled all-glass iPhone, while evaluating potential price increases for upcoming models.

items.title: Apple gets downgraded, Intel plans to raise $15B: AlphaSpace check
items.summary: Yahoo Finance Markets and Data Editor Jared Blikre uses the AlphaSpace platform to take a closer look at some of Monday's trending stories: Apple (AAPL) getting a downgrade and Intel's (INTC) plan to raise $15 billion through stock offerings. items.title: Micron is Gaining Share. These Bulls See More Upside Ahead
items.summary: Bulls are stacking up price targets that tower above current levels while a famous short seller is betting against the memory giant. The case for each side is stronger than you might expect.

items.summary: Three businesses have quietly turned patient shareholders into millionaires over multiple decades, and the competitive moats that drove those returns are facing their biggest tests yet in 2026.

items.title: Apple’s Dip Below $310 is a Great Accumulation Opportunity
items.summary: Apple just posted its strongest June quarter ever, yet the stock sits 7% lower and traders put even odds on it closing August above $310. Here is why that tension could matter more than the headline numbers.

items.title: With a New iPhone Coming, Here’s What $10,000 in Apple Since the First One Is Worth
items.summary: Apple is approaching another iPhone launch with a $4.5 trillion market cap and nearly two decades of stock gains that have crushed the broader market at every turn. The question now is whether that compounding machine still has room to run or if the law of large numbers finally catches up.

items.summary: Berkshire has finally started to put its cash to work.

items.title: Klarna Group (KLAR) Will Provide Leasing For A New US Device Upgrade Program
items.summary: Klarna Group (NYSE:KLAR) is providing the leasing and financing backbone for Apple's new Apple Upgrade program in the United States. The partnership integrates Klarna into one of Apple's core hardware ownership offerings, expanding Klarna's exposure to US Apple customers. The role places Klarna more directly in consumer electronics financing beyond its existing buy now, pay later services. This kind of tie up is only one way to gain exposure to stable consumer themes.
